## Placement Palette

The source rail of things not yet placed.

```gts
<PlacementPalette
  @items={{this.items}}
  @placements={{@model.draft}}
  @searchable={{true}}
  @heading='Author'
/>
```

### Why this is the piece kanban does not have

On a kanban board every card already sits in a column — there is no "not yet anywhere" state to render, so no rail is needed. A placement board starts with a pool and an **empty** plan, and the rail is where the remaining work is visible. It shrinks as the plan fills, which is the progress signal; a separate "3 of 12 placed" counter would only repeat what the rail already shows.

### Args

| Arg | What it does |
|---|---|
| `items` | The candidates. Required. |
| `placements` | What is already on the board. Placed items leave the rail, so it always reads as "what is left to do". |
| `keepPlaced` | Keep placed items visible but dimmed instead of removing them — for a board used as a review surface rather than a work surface. |
| `onDragStart` | Fires after the payload is written, so a host can mirror the drag elsewhere. |
| `onSelect` | Chip click. |
| `groupBy` | Bucket by `item.group`. |
| `searchable` | Show the search box. |
| `heading`, `emptyLabel` | Copy. |

`:chip` block replaces a chip's content while keeping the chip chrome.

### `PlacementItem` is not a CardDef

```ts
interface PlacementItem { id: string; title: string; group?: string; detail?: string; hue?: string }
```

Deliberately a plain shape. The family works for things that are not cards — a seat number, an SKU, a row from an import — and a host that *does* have cards passes `id: card.id` and keeps its own lookup. This is what stops the rail from needing to know how to render every card type in the realm.

### The drag handshake

The module exports the DataTransfer key both ends use:

```ts
export const PLACEMENT_DRAG_TYPE = 'application/x-boxel-placement';
```

A drop zone imports it rather than retyping the string, so a rename cannot silently break the handshake — the failure would otherwise be a drop that does nothing, with no error anywhere.

Two payloads are written on every drag: the private type carries the id for our own drop zones, and `text/plain` keeps the drag legible to anything else on the page and to the browser's own drag image.

### Two empty states, never one message

"Everything is placed" and "nothing matches your search" are different outcomes — one is success, the other is a dead end the user fixes by clearing the search. A shared "No items" would make the second look like the first. A third message covers a genuinely empty pool.

### Group order is first-seen, not alphabetical

The host's own ordering usually carries meaning — seniority, priority, floor number — and re-sorting would destroy it silently.

### Responsive

`container-type: inline-size`. Below 180px the secondary detail line is dropped rather than wrapped, because a two-line chip halves how many fit on screen and the rail's whole value is seeing what is left at a glance.

### Example

`PlacementPaletteExample/crew-week` groups six crew by role with two already placed, so the rail shows only what is left.

### Non-goals

Does not own the placements — it reads them to decide what to hide. Does not decide where an item lands; that is the drop zone's job. Not a card picker: use a card chooser when the task is finding one card, not distributing many.
